summary: I re-reviewed the three repaired files and found no remaining BLOCKER or MAJOR issues. The materializer now explicitly sorts NULL `lastMaterializedAt` values first (`{ sort: "asc", nulls: "first" }`) and breaks ties by id. Because of that, new identities can't be starved behind 100+ identities that were already processed. The confirmation still requires an upcoming live and an identity that has never been materialized. All three registration events (confirmation, reminder, live_started) now use the injected time as `dueAt`. The UI text now discloses that saving a confirmation template also skips bindings made before that save that haven't been processed yet. That matches the explicit-disclosure fix accepted earlier, and the remaining first-observation behavior matches the stated contract. The text splitter's 5-chunk limit, its 5000-unit-per-chunk limit and its grapheme packing are correct. One MINOR issue remains: the URL pattern also captures the text after a URL, which affects packing in rare cases. This finding comes only from reading the supplied text. I did not run any tests, so it doesn't confirm that tests or a release succeed.

findings.issue: `\S+` matches until the next whitespace. In Chinese copy, the text after a URL usually has no space (for example `{{live_url}}，請準時進場…`), so the URL token also takes in the punctuation and all the Chinese text up to the next space or newline. That whole span is treated as one piece that is never split at grapheme boundaries.
findings.evidence: `for (const token of text.split(/(https?:\/\/\S+)/gu))` followed by `if (/^https?:\/\//u.test(token)) { if (!append(token)) return null; continue; }`. `append` returns false whenever `part.length > 5000`. The comment says URLs are recognized after Chinese copy, but nothing stops the match before Chinese text that follows the URL.
findings.impact: If a URL is directly followed by a long Chinese paragraph with no whitespace, that text can't be packed into the space left in the current bubble. This wastes bubble space and can push a message that would fit into 5 bubbles over the limit, so it returns null. If the combined span is over 5000 UTF-16 units, the function always returns null and the merchant's notification is suppressed. This only happens with unusual templates. It never truncates text or splits a surrogate pair.
findings.recommended_fix: End URL tokens at whitespace and at CJK or full-width characters and punctuation. For example: `/(https?:\/\/[^\s　-〿㐀-鿿＀-￯]+)/gu`, or `[\x21-\x7E]+` for ASCII-only URLs. Any text after the URL then goes through the grapheme packing path.
findings.required_test: Build the input `https://example.com/x` + `，` + 4990 CJK characters (no whitespace), plus enough other text that grapheme packing fits in 5 bubbles but atomic URL handling does not. Assert that the result is not null, that every chunk is ≤5000 units, that the URL is never split across chunks, and that joining the chunks reproduces the original text.
